author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Massachusetts’ highest court publicly reprimanded Judge Shelley Joseph on Thursday, closing a disciplinary case that grew out of allegations that a defendant avoided a federal immigration arrest at a Newton courthouse in 2018.

Federal prosecutors charged Joseph in 2019 and dropped the case in 2022 after she agreed to face a state disciplinary review. Prosecutors had alleged that a Dominican man appearing before her was allowed to leave through a rear courthouse door while an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent waited elsewhere in the building.

A disciplinary hearing officer later found that the Judicial Conduct Commission had not proved Joseph knew of a plan to help the defendant evade ICE. The commission ultimately sought a public reprimand rather than suspension or removal.

In a unanimous unsigned opinion, the Supreme Judicial Court found separate violations of judicial conduct rules. It cited an off-the-record discussion with the defendant’s lawyer and Joseph’s suggestion that the man might be held overnight after she learned an ICE officer was present. The court said those actions created an improper appearance even though the alleged knowing role in an escape plan was not established.
dek: The state’s Supreme Judicial Court imposed a public reprimand while emphasizing that investigators did not prove the judge knew of an evasion plan.
headline: Massachusetts high court reprimands judge in ICE courthouse case
